canonical_statement: Let n >= 2 and let Omega be a bounded domain in R^n with the regularity required for the zero-boundary Sobolev space. There are constants alpha > 0 and C < infinity, depending on n and Omega, such that every u in W_0^{1,n}(Omega) with integral_Omega |grad u|^n <= 1 satisfies integral_Omega exp(alpha * |u|^(n/(n-1))) <= C.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat with 2 <= n; Omega a bounded sufficiently regular measurable domain in EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n); u in the zero-trace Sobolev space W_0^{1,n}(Omega); Prop in Lean universe 0 (provisional)
quantifiers: Omega subset R^n, bounded and with the source-required domain regularity
there exist alpha : Real and C : Real with 0 < alpha and 0 <= C
for every u in W_0^{1,n}(Omega) whose gradient L^n energy is at most 1
hypotheses: Omega is bounded and satisfies the domain assumptions fixed by the primary-source audit
u has zero boundary trace and weak gradient in L^n(Omega)
integral over Omega of |grad u|^n is at most 1
conclusion: integral over Omega of exp(alpha * |u|^(n/(n-1))) is at most C
